name: event-emitter
description: Implement a custom event emitter with on, off, emit, and once methods

promptLevels.intermediate: implement an EventEmitter class with on, off, and emit methods
promptLevels.advanced: create an EventEmitter class with on(event, callback), off(event, callback), emit(event, ...args), and once(event, callback) methods
promptLevels.expert: Implement an `EventEmitter` class with: `on(event: string, callback: Function): void` to subscribe, `off(event: string, callback: Function): void` to unsubscribe, `emit(event: string, ...args: any[]): void` to trigger callbacks, and `once(event: string, callback: Function): void` for single-fire subscriptions. {languageSpecific}

languageInstructions.typescript: Use TypeScript with proper type annotations. Consider using generics or a callback type. Export only the EventEmitter class.
languageInstructions.javascript: Use JavaScript. Store listeners in a Map or object. Export only the EventEmitter class.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Use JavaScript with JSDoc annotations for all methods. Document parameter types and return values. Export only the EventEmitter class.

variants.typescript: Implement an `EventEmitter` class in TypeScript with proper type annotations. Methods: `on(event: string, callback: Function): void`, `off(event: string, callback: Function): void`, `emit(event: string, ...args: any[]): void`, `once(event: string, callback: Function): void`. Export only the EventEmitter class.
variants.javascript: Implement an `EventEmitter` class in JavaScript. Methods: `on(event, callback)`, `off(event, callback)`, `emit(event, ...args)`, `once(event, callback)`. Export only the EventEmitter class.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: Implement an `EventEmitter` class in JavaScript with full JSDoc annotations. Document all methods with @param and @return tags. Export only the EventEmitter class.

testCases.test: const ee = new EventEmitter(); let called = false; ee.on('test', () => { called = true; }); ee.emit('test'); console.assert(called === true, 'Callback should be called on emit');
const ee = new EventEmitter(); let value = 0; ee.on('add', (n) => { value += n; }); ee.emit('add', 5); ee.emit('add', 3); console.assert(value === 8, 'Should pass arguments to callback');

const ee = new EventEmitter(); let count = 0; const cb = () => { count++; }; ee.on('test', cb); ee.emit('test'); ee.off('test', cb); ee.emit('test'); console.assert(count === 1, 'off should remove listener');
const ee = new EventEmitter(); let count = 0; ee.once('test', () => { count++; }); ee.emit('test'); ee.emit('test'); console.assert(count === 1, 'once should only fire once');

const ee = new EventEmitter(); let results = []; ee.on('test', (a, b) => { results.push(a + b); }); ee.emit('test', 1, 2); ee.emit('test', 3, 4); console.assert(results[0] === 3 && results[1] === 7, 'Should handle multiple args');
